items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: I got an offer from Earl Heinz.

ctx.x: Like to do it. Uh, who all did you get offers from? What were some of the different people?

I got an offer from Earl Heinz. Who want me to come up? Uh. Yeah. Got off. Uh. Oliver wanted me to come up there with him. I wouldn't leave though. And then we had this fellow, Fat Wallace. He wanted me to come up with him. But I wasn't going no way.
Well, how did Fat Wallace know you? Fat used to come down here often.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Because tonight I played against Earl Hines down there. And Earl Hines had a good band in them days.

ctx.x: Well, when you had a contest, would the other band play the same tune or what? How would that work?

No, no. They'd play what they want. They'd play what they wanted. They'd play the best they got. They'd play what they wanted to. You don't have to play just what they play. Sometimes accidentally you play a number they played already, or they're going to play, something like that. But you don't have to play. You just play what you think you can play best. Best super for your band, that's what you play. Because tonight I played against Earl Hines down there. And Earl Hines had a good band in them days. He was a…

take me a couple of shots and I begin to call some numbers. I'll begin to blow a little bit. Take me a couple of more shots. And just give me that drum, that piano, and bass. Then I'll get the people over here. Just clap your hand, I'll bring the people here. Well around 1.30 I had Earl Hines over there, let alone all the people. Had him over there. Him and his whole band, because I know that boy was playing first alto with him, I knew him better. He's a fine guy, he played violin too.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: Yeah, I met him when he came down here.

ctx.x: Let me just ask you one thing about the Pelican that I meant to ask you. You say you had three or four nights a month there. Yeah. That's all you had, three or four nights a month? Yeah. So it was one night a week, huh?

Yeah, maybe one night a week, yeah. Did you keep filling in with other jobs with that? Well, yeah, yeah. I guess you have to. We kept filling in with other jobs. The first man met... Ben met Earl Heinz's band when he came down here. At this time. Yeah, and he had a troubled band. Yeah, I met him when he came down here. And met... Clayborne Williams. What do you mean met him? You played opposite of what? Yeah, I played opposite. I played on one standing, then played on the other. Yeah. Mm-hmm. Well, that was most…
So who did you get into the band when Don Albert took, Albert and what you call him?
